images.title: Two boxes make one hour
images.purpose: Shows how a block of boxes on the 48 box strip gives the start time and the length of an activity.
images.composition: Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no characters, no extra text. One long strip of 48 boxes across the centre, one block coloured, with times under the strip and a bracket over the block.
images.exact_structure: A single row of 48 equal boxes with thin grey (#6B7280) outlines, all white except boxes 20 to 33, which are filled amber (#E69F00), 14 boxes. Under the left edge of box 1 and under the right edge of box 48: midnight. Under the line between box 24 and box 25: noon. Under the left edge of box 20: 9:30 am. Under the right edge of box 33: 4:30 pm. Above the amber block, a reddish purple (#CC79A7) bracket labelled 14 boxes = 7 hours. Above box 1, a small teal (#0072B2) brace over that single box labelled 1 box = 30 minutes.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Each box is 30 minutes, so 14 boxes of school are 7 hours, starting at box 20.
images.description: Shows how a block of boxes on the 48 box strip gives the start time and the length of an activity.
images.context: Box n starts (n − 1) × 30 minutes after midnight: box 20 starts at 9:30 am; box 33 ends at 4:30 pm.

image_decisions.why: A 48 box strip with one block counted shows how boxes turn into clock times and hours.
